topic_summary: Analysis of free movement within the European Union as a contested kernel of federation-membership commitment. The shared commitment to federation-membership is read as either integration-primary (supranational authority, labor mobility as core right) or member-sovereignty-primary (national authority, border control as residual power). Each reading instantiates a different constraint structure with divergent cost-bearers and legitimacy grounds.

key_entities: European Union (supranational federation with free movement provisions)
Member States (27 sovereign states with treaty obligations)
Schengen Area (borderless zone subset of EU)
European Court of Justice (treaty interpretation authority)
Mobile EU Citizens (workers exercising free movement rights)
Local Labor Markets (destination-state workers facing wage/employment competition)
key_tensions: Supranational treaty authority vs member-state constitutional sovereignty
Labor mobility rights vs local labor market protection
Integration deepening vs opt-out/exit dynamics (Brexit as revealed preference)
key_mechanisms: Treaty of Maastricht Article 21 (free movement as fundamental right)
ECJ preliminary ruling procedure (member court → ECJ → binding interpretation)
Emergency border control provisions (temporary Schengen suspension for public order)
key_absences: Fiscal transfer mechanism to compensate destination regions for public service costs
Exit cost asymmetry: high-emigration states lose tax base without treaty revision mechanism

axes.structural_delta: Federation-membership kernel read as irreversible integration commitment; supranational authority legitimate; free movement as constitutional right immune to member-state override
axes.primary_observable: ECJ ruling pattern (member restrictions struck down); treaty amendment threshold (unanimity); political rhetoric treating restriction as illegitimate
axes.selection_reason: First reading: integration-primary interpretation; victim set includes local workers; high ε from labor market displacement

axes.structural_delta: Federation-membership kernel read as conditional treaty; national authority retains legitimacy over borders; free movement as negotiable policy rather than constitutional right
axes.primary_observable: Emergency border closure frequency; political viability of unilateral restriction; Brexit as exit-right exercise; polling on national vs EU authority
axes.selection_reason: Second reading: sovereignty-primary interpretation; inverted victim/beneficiary structure; same observable domain (border/mobility) but opposite constraint

axes.human_readable: Fiscal Federalism Absence (No Compensatory Transfer Mechanism)
axes.structural_delta: EU lacks fiscal transfer mechanism to offset public service costs in high-immigration regions or tax base loss in high-emigration regions
axes.primary_observable: EU budget allocation; absence of formula-based regional compensation; member-state fiscal burden data
axes.selection_reason: Third axis: structural absence that would mediate between readings; snare that makes integration-reading costs visible; downstream of reading choice

axes.human_readable: Exit Cost Asymmetry (High-Emigration State Tax Base Loss)
axes.structural_delta: Eastern EU states lose skilled workers and tax base to western states without treaty mechanism for labor-export compensation
axes.primary_observable: Net migration flows by skill level; source-state public investment vs destination-state benefit capture
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: overlaps with fiscal_federalism_absence; lower centrality; both are downstream costs of integration reading

axes.human_readable: Schengen Opt-Out as Scaffold (Partial Exit Without Full Secession)
axes.structural_delta: Ireland/Cyprus non-participation in Schengen; UK pre-Brexit opt-out; demonstrates federation membership divisible from free movement commitment
axes.primary_observable: Opt-out treaty provisions; border control retention by non-Schengen members
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: scaffold supporting sovereignty_reading but adds limited structural novelty; opt-out existence already embedded in sovereignty constraint story

deferred_axes.structural_delta: High-emigration states lose tax base without compensation mechanism
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Overlaps with fiscal_federalism_absence; both are downstream snares of integration reading with similar victim sets

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Opt-out provisions demonstrate membership divisibility from free movement
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Scaffold adds limited novelty; opt-out existence embedded in sovereignty_reading constraint logic

omegas.description: Does Brexit reveal the federation-membership kernel as rope (negotiable treaty) rather than mountain (irreversible integration)? If member exit is institutionally feasible, integration_reading's claimed permanence is normative rather than structural.
omegas.source: Tension 3 (Brexit as revealed preference) + Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium)

omegas.description: What grounds ECJ interpretive authority if member states retain constitutional sovereignty? Integration_reading treats ECJ as final arbiter; sovereignty_reading treats it as delegated agent revocable by principals. Authority grounding determines which reading is structurally coherent.
omegas.source: Mechanism 2 (ECJ preliminary ruling) + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: Would fiscal transfer mechanism eliminate tension between readings or merely shift cost-bearer identity? If compensation is structurally feasible, fiscal_federalism_absence is piton (policy choice) not snare (structural trap).

Is there a coherent third reading that treats free movement as qualified right (neither absolute nor fully discretionary)? Proportionality doctrine in ECJ case law may instantiate hybrid reading not captured in binary framework.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + F15 (Premature Closure)

fracture_scan.notes: F15 detected: binary reading framework may miss proportionality-based third reading visible in ECJ case law. Generated omega_third_reading_hybrid. F03 detected: fiscal_federalism_absence classified as snare but may be piton if compensation is policy choice not structural impossibility. Generated omega_compensatory_mechanism_feasibility.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Federation-membership commitment binding EU member states to supranational authority and free movement provisions
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested between ECJ treaty interpretation (integration reading) and residual member-state constitutional sovereignty (sovereignty reading)

readings.commitment: Federation-membership as irreversible integration; supranational authority legitimate; free movement as constitutional right
readings.authority_grounding: ECJ interpretive supremacy; treaty as constitutional document
readings.expected_structural_delta: Mobile citizens in beneficiary set; local labor markets in victim set; high ε from labor displacement; border restriction illegitimate

readings.commitment: Federation-membership as conditional treaty; national authority retains border legitimacy; free movement as negotiable policy
readings.authority_grounding: Member-state constitutional sovereignty; treaty as revocable delegation
readings.expected_structural_delta: Local labor markets in beneficiary set; mobile citizens in victim set; high ε from mobility restriction; border control legitimate

axiom_contradictions.basis: Integration reading's axiom (supranational authority as constitutionally supreme) requires rejecting sovereignty reading's axiom (national sovereignty as residual and revocable). No single coherent framework holds both: either treaty binds states irrevocably (integration) or states retain exit/override authority (sovereignty).
